newsitem.title: USA: Brinkley chat with "bore" Clinton now up in air.
newsitem.headline: Brinkley chat with "bore" Clinton now up in air.

text.p: Forget the election results, what Americans buzzed about on Thursday was whether President Clinton will grant an interview with David Brinkley after the famed broadcaster called him a "bore" on air.
The White House would not say and Brinkley's employer, ABC News, said it did not know and was awaiting word.

The interview was tentatively set before the election for Friday so that it could be aired on Sunday on "This Week with David Brinkley," which is the 76-year-old Brinkley's last show as host of the programme for 15 years. He will remain as a commentator on the programme but had hoped the interview would be a highlight of his move into semi-retirement.
But that was before early Wednesday morning when he slammed Clinton in a final summation during the wrap-up of ABC's live election coverage.
Brinkley complimented his colleagues on their creativity, but said said "Clinton ... has not a creative bone in his body. Therefore he is a bore and will always be a bore."
That came on top on his predicting that the second Clinton administration will be "four more years ... of nonsense" and calling Clinton's victory statement "one of the worst things I've ever heard."
Theories abounded the next day that Brinkley may not have realised he was on the air, but ABC said that he did.

Brinkley's comments were widely reported and, at one point on Wednesday, was the second item on the radio broadcast of a rival network -- right after the election results. The TV tabloid shows have been having a field day playing and replaying the tape.
White House Press secretary Mike McCurry hemmed and hawed when asked whether the president would give an interview to Brinkley.

Asked whether he was saying "yes or no," McCurry said, "In other words I'm not going to say." He added that decisions on Sunday talks shows are not made until Friday and "to my knowledge he (Brinkley) has not clarified those remarks."
An ABC spokeswoman said that as of 5 P.M. EST Thursday there was no confirmation that an interview would take place.
She added, "The interview was never completely confirmed and never officially booked. Nothing was ever confirmed. If we don't get it, we will do something else."
Brinkley was not available for comment and cancelled at least one TV talk show.
